To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the longitudinal electron polarization in the beta decay of polarized nuclei can be used to search for right-handed currents, and that the sensitivity of this search can be improved by using a polarized positron beam.

the beta polarization of a polarized nuclear target can be measured without an absolute calibration of either of the two polarization vectors, that the beta polarization can be used as a probe of the weak interaction, and that the beta polarization is sensitive to right handed currents in the weak interactions.

(i) the longitudinal electron or positronic beta polarization is sensitive to right-hand current contributions in the beta decay of polarized nuclei, (ii) the sensitivity is not reduced by the need for an absolute calibration of either beta polarimeter or nuclear polarization, and (iii) the sensitivity is enhanced by the use of a beta polarimeter that has a large acceptance for the beta rays
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the weak interaction by means of beta-decay correlation experiments.
the development and application of new techniques in the study of the structure of matter and of the weak interaction.
the study of the weak interactions of elementary particles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the experimental data do not rule out the presence of right-handed currents in beta decay, but that the data do rule out the possibility of a pure right-handed current.
the experimental evidence is consistent with the standard V-A theory and is incompatible with pure V+A theory.
there is no evidence of right-handed currents at a level greater than 10(-4) to 10(-5).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the sensitivity to right-handed currents of the longitudinal polarization of electrons in the beta decay of polarized nuclei has not been fully explored.
we are able to measure the longitudinal polarization of the beta decay electrons and positrons from the decay of the oriented nuclei 6He and 8Li, respectively.
we have developed a technique that can be used in the future to search for a right handed component in the weak interaction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a measurement of the polarization of the beta decay electrons in the decay of polarized nuclei can provide a new constraint on the existence of right-handed currents in weak interactions.
the beta polarimeter does not have to be calibrated absolutely.
the beta polarization correlation is sensitive to right- and left-handed currents in the decay, and that this correlation is a function of the nuclear polarization direction.
